post.title: You Can't Explain How a Zipper Works #shorts
post.description: Could you explain it? Tell me in the comments. Send this to your know-it-all friend. Dev is sure he knows exactly how a zipper works, until Theo says: explain it. In 'The Misunderstood Limits of Folk Science: An Illusion of Explanatory Depth' (Cognitive Science, 2002), Leonid Rozenblit and Frank Keil had Yale students rate how well they understood everyday devices, then write step-by-step explanations of how they work. After explaining, their ratings of their own understanding dropped. Psychologists call it the illusion of explanatory depth: things we use every day feel understood because they feel familiar. Using isn't knowing, and that's fine. #psychology #shorts #overconfidence #learning #overthinking

Explain how your fridge stays cold. Go. Yeah, EXACTLY.
